1. Visão Geral do AplicativoDesenvolver um aplicativo móvel nativo/híbrido (iOS e Android) com dois perfis de usuário principais: Cliente (Usuário) e Administrador (Salão de Beleza). O objetivo principal é digitalizar e otimizar o processo de agendamento, permitindo que os clientes reservem serviços de forma autônoma e que o administrador gerencie a agenda e a comunicação de maneira eficiente.2. Requisitos por PerfilA. Perfil do Cliente (Usuário)O cliente deve ter uma experiência intuitiva e completa para agendar e gerenciar seus próprios serviços.FuncionalidadeDescriçãoCadastro/LoginCadastro rápido (e-mail, Google, Facebook) e login seguro.Exploração de ServiçosVisualização de uma lista completa de serviços (corte, coloração, manicure, etc.) com descrição detalhada, duração e preço.Agendamento1. B. Deve incluir um template com os detalhes do agendamento.Configuração de HorárioDefinição dos horários de funcionamento do salão, feriados e bloqueios de agenda.Relatórios BásicosGeração de relatórios simples de agendamentos realizados (por período e por profissional).Status do AgendamentoO administrador deve poder alterar o status de um agendamento (Ex: Agendado, Confirmado, Em Atendimento, Concluído, Cancelado).

**Conceptualizing the Architecture**

I'm currently focused on the overarching architecture, mapping out the distinct functionalities required for both Client and Administrator roles. I've begun to break down the features for each, starting with Client features like account creation, appointment scheduling, and service browsing. Simultaneously, I'm considering Administrator features such as managing services, staff schedules, and client records. My aim is to define the core data models and API endpoints.


**Mapping Out Features & Tech**

I've just finalized the basic user flows for both Client and Admin roles. For clients, it's pretty standard: sign up/login, browse, book, view/manage appointments. Admins get CRUD controls over services, staff, and schedules, plus reports and some communication tools. I'm leaning towards React Context + `localStorage` for state management since there's no backend. The tech stack is set: React, TypeScript, Tailwind, Lucide for icons, `date-fns` for dates, and `recharts` for charts. I'm exploring potential uses for Gemini API, maybe for automating descriptions or analyzing reviews.


**Considering User Flows & AI**

I've been thinking about the application's flow, especially concerning the routing. Although I initially considered a custom state-based router for simplicity, given the project's evolving complexity, I've opted for `HashRouter` from `react-router-dom` for navigation. I'm also actively considering Gemini API integration points. For clients, perhaps an AI-powered service recommendation engine, and for admins, features like smart reply generation or sentiment analysis are possibilities. I'm focusing on defining core UI/UX elements, like distinct layouts for client and admin roles, and a mobile-first design.

I've just finalized the mock data schemas: `Service`, `Professional`, `Appointment`, and `User`. With the data structure defined, I'm now outlining the implementation plan in steps. Step 1 will cover setup and boilerplate. Step 2 concentrates on shared components like buttons and layouts. Step 3 focuses on service logic and mock data to load the initial state. In step 4, I'll tackle the client side, focusing on user authentication and client-specific functionality.


**Building Core Features**

Right now, I'm working on the foundational views. I've designed the authentication screen with admin/client toggles. For clients, the core flow is in place: browse services, select professionals and slots, and confirm appointments. I'm focusing on "My Appointments" next with a cancel option. For admins, I'm building a dashboard and a calendar view. Services and professional management screens are underway, along with Gemini API tools, such as the "Smart Message Generator" for automating WhatsApp reminders.


**Constructing Core Data & Context**

I've just added the base structure for role and status enums, along with the UI structure defined at the highest level: The main application has state for users, services, appointments, etc. and it passes this state down via `AppDataContext`. I'm starting work on the `index.html` file, including Tailwind CDN and Inter font, defining types and creating mock data. Now starting to build out the `AppContext` with a Google Gen AI service wrapper.


**Defining Admin Features & Polish**

I'm now implementing the admin features, specifically the dashboard and CRUD screens. I've integrated Gemini API with `gemini-2.5-flash` for faster text generation, enabling admins to generate friendly appointment reminders with a single click. I'm focusing on ensuring a polished and accessible UI, paying close attention to Tailwind classes, shadows, and contrast. I've also added a login screen to easily switch between client and admin roles. I've decided on the final file structure to keep things organized.


**Organizing Components & Code**

I've just been refining the file structure for optimal development. Now, I'm consolidating shared components into `components/Shared.tsx` for easy access. All client-specific logic will live in `pages/ClientViews.tsx`, and admin logic will reside in `pages/AdminViews.tsx`, helping the code be more manageable. Focusing on the "active communication" feature, I'll generate the relevant link (either `mailto` or `wa.me`) and use Gemini to craft the message body with appointment details, enabling users to copy-paste the message. I'm currently focused on the overarching goal: integrating a database into "BeautyBook Pro." Right now, the app uses mock data, which has limitations. I'm exploring the best database options and how to seamlessly integrate it, minimizing disruption to existing features. I'm prioritizing user experience and data integrity throughout this transition.


**Choosing IndexedDB Solution**

I've determined that IndexedDB is the best fit. Given the frontend-only constraint, it provides persistent, transactional storage directly in the browser. This eliminates the need for external server dependencies. I'm focusing on crafting the IndexedDB integration in a way that minimizes impact on the existing `mockData.ts` and `AppContext.tsx` implementation. The goal is a smooth transition with enhanced data management.


**Exploring Local Storage Wrapper**

I'm now considering a custom `localStorage` wrapper, instead of IndexedDB. The goal is simplicity and a minimal-dependency implementation. This wrapper will emulate asynchronous API calls for a smooth user experience. The asynchronous nature will simulate network delays, while also preserving data across browser reloads. This approach allows a streamlined "drop-in" replacement for the current mock data implementation. I aim to achieve a seamless user experience that is also easy to maintain and expand.


**Developing Persistence Layer**

The persistence layer is now a priority. I'm creating a `db.ts` file to manage data persistence using `localStorage` as a foundation. It will initialize from the mock data if no data exists. This will make it robust enough for a prototype and persist across browser reloads. I'm focusing on methods like `getServices`, `saveService`, and similar functions to handle appointments and services. Using `async/await` will simulate a real API experience. I will update `AppContext.tsx` to utilize this new `db.ts` file, loading and saving data.


**Finalizing Database Operations**

I'm solidifying the database interactions. The structure of `db.ts` is coming together, with `STORAGE_KEYS` defined and `init()` handling initial data. Methods like `findAll`, `save`, `update`, and `delete` are shaping up nicely. The goal is now to refactor the `AppContext.tsx` to use this new `db.ts` layer effectively, ensuring all data operations go through the database abstraction. This design will create a clean and maintainable architecture.


**Constructing Persistence Layer**

I'm now fully immersed in the coding phase, building the persistence layer with `localStorage`.  I'm focusing on emulating a repository pattern within `db.ts`, making it feel like a real database interaction. Key methods are in place for the services, professionals, appointments, and config data types. Crucially, I'm incorporating an `init` phase that leverages the mock data to populate the storage on first run. Also, to improve user experience and mimic real API behavior, I've added a simulated 500ms network delay to make the loaders more obvious. I'm updating `AppContext.tsx` with asynchronous `loadData` functionality and an `isLoading` flag.


**Adapting UI To New DB**

I'm now integrating the new database interactions throughout the UI. I'm updating components like `login`, `addAppointment`, and others to use the `db` functions consistently. Error handling is paramount, so I'm wrapping all database operations in `try/catch` blocks to provide graceful error management.  I'm also removing the "fake delay" from the `SettingsManager` since the new database service has its own simulated network delay. This approach keeps the UI consistent and responsive.


**Integrating New Data Flow**

The core focus now is on integrating the new data flow. I'm updating `AppContext` to align with the database interactions. Previously, updates were synchronous.  Now, I'm making calls to the database and awaiting the result, then updating state. The goal is to ensure UI consistency with the persistence layer.  I'm also ensuring that `loadData` is called on mount and that appointments persist in the database. Furthermore, I'll clearly define this as a "Persistent Local Database" to accurately reflect the implementation strategy.


**Validating Data Integration**

I'm now focusing on integrating `db.ts` fully and ensuring it works seamlessly. I'm importing the necessary constants from `mockData.ts` and types from `types.ts` into `db.ts`. I'm also importing the `db` methods into `AppContext.tsx`. The goal is to fully replace the mock data with the persistent storage layer. I'm verifying data retrieval and updates through the UI to ensure a robust and functional application.

Como não temos um servidor backend disponível neste ambiente (Node.js, Python, etc.), a melhor abordagem para "integrar um banco de dados" que persista os dados mesmo após recarregar a página é criar uma camada de **Simulação de Banco de Dados Persistente** usando o LocalStorage do navegador, mas estruturada profissionalmente com Padrão Repository e chamadas Assíncronas (Promises).

Isso fará o app se comportar exatamente como se estivesse conectado a uma API real, mantendo os dados salvos.

Aqui está a especificação da solução:

1.  **Criar `services/db.ts`**:
    *   Este serviço atuará como o "cliente do banco de dados".
    *   Ele inicializará os dados com o `mockData.ts` na primeira vez que o app for aberto.
    *   Terá métodos assíncronos (`get`, `create`, `update`, `delete`) para cada entidade (Agendamentos, Serviços, Profissionais, Configurações).
    *   Simulará um pequeno "delay" de rede para dar feedback visual de carregamento real.

2.  **Atualizar `contexts/AppContext.tsx`**:
    *   Substituirá a inicialização direta dos mocks por um `useEffect` que carrega os dados do `db.ts`.
    *   Todas as funções de modificação (`addAppointment`, `updateService`, etc.) agora serão `async` e aguardarão a confirmação do "banco de dados" antes de atualizar a tela.

3.  **Resultado**:
    *   Se você agendar um cliente, recarregar a página, o agendamento continuará lá.
    *   Se você alterar o horário de funcionamento, ele persistirá.

### Passo 1: Escolher o Provedor

*   **Firebase:** Melhor para escalabilidade rápida e dados em tempo real (WebSockets).

### Passo 2: Instalar o SDK

Você precisaria adicionar a biblioteca do banco escolhido no seu `package.json` (ou no `importmap` no caso deste projeto sem bundler complexo).

```javascript
import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
```

### Passo 3: Configurar Variáveis de Ambiente

```typescript
},
```

### Esquema do Banco de Dados (SQL)

Você pode rodar este script no "SQL Editor" do Supabase ou em qualquer cliente PostgreSQL.

```sql
-- 1. ENUMS (Para Status e Funções)
CREATE TYPE user_role AS ENUM ('CLIENT', 'ADMIN');
CREATE TYPE appointment_status AS ENUM ('PENDING', 'CONFIRMED', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'COMPLETED', 'CANCELLED');

-- 2. TABELA DE USUÁRIOS (Perfis)
-- Geralmente vinculada à tabela de autenticação do provedor (ex: auth.users no Supabase)
CREATE TABLE profiles (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  full_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  role user_role DEFAULT 'CLIENT',
  avatar_url TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- 3. TABELA DE SERVIÇOS
CREATE TABLE services (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  duration_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 60,
  price DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  image_url TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- 4. TABELA DE PROFISSIONAIS
CREATE TABLE professionals (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  avatar_url TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- 5. TABELA PIVÔ (Muitos-para-Muitos: Profissionais <-> Serviços)
-- Define quais serviços cada profissional sabe fazer (specialties)
CREATE TABLE professional_services (
  professional_id UUID REFERENCES professionals(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  service_id UUID REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  PRIMARY KEY (professional_id, service_id)
);

-- 6. TABELA DE AGENDAMENTOS
CREATE TABLE appointments (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Pode ser nulo se o admin criar para alguém sem conta
  service_id UUID REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  professional_id UUID REFERENCES professionals(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  
  -- Dados do Cliente (Snapshots para histórico ou convidados)
  client_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  client_phone TEXT,
  client_email TEXT,
  
  -- Dados do Agendamento
  appointment_date DATE NOT NULL,
  appointment_time TIME NOT NULL,
  status appointment_status DEFAULT 'PENDING',
  
  -- Avaliação
  rating INTEGER CHECK (rating >= 1 AND rating <= 5),
  review_comment TEXT,
  
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- 7. TABELA DE CONFIGURAÇÃO DE HORÁRIOS (Business Config)
-- Terá 7 linhas (0 = Domingo a 6 = Sábado)
CREATE TABLE business_hours (
  day_of_week INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (day_of_week BETWEEN 0 AND 6),
  is_open BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
  start_time TIME DEFAULT '09:00',
  end_time TIME DEFAULT '18:00',
  has_lunch BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  lunch_start TIME DEFAULT '12:00',
  lunch_end TIME DEFAULT '13:00'
);
```
